subject: maths
question: P can do a piece of work in 30 days and Q can do the same work in 40 days. They worked together for 5 days and then Q left. How much time (in days and hours) will P, working alone, take to complete the remaining work?
solution:
**Given:**

P can do a piece of work in 30 days 

Q can do the same work in 40 days

They worked together for 5 days and then Q left

**Concept used:**

Efficiency = (Total work / Total time taken)

Efficiency = work done in a single day 

**Calculation:**

Let total work is 120 units ( LCM of 30 and 40) 

The efficiency of P = 120/30

⇒ 4 units

The efficiency of Q = 120/40

⇒ 3 units

So P + Q together do in one day 4 + 3 = 7 units

So they do in 5 days 7 × 5 = 35 units

Remaining, 120 - 35 = 85 units done by P 

P does the work in 85 / 4 = 21(1)/(4) days

⇒ 21 days 6 hours

**∴ P take to complete the remaining work is 21 days 6 hours.**
